sentences.en: I think, for me, probably the funniest part and the hardest part to hold it together was when I said to him that he couldn't just sit there and cry.

sentences.en: But I think that's part of the fun of it.

sentences.en: I mean, it was kind of, like, everything that I thought that I wanted it to be, it was.

sentences.en: And I remember talking to my friend who was, like, my main friend that we loved The Office together.

sentences.en: And he's like, you're kidding me, you know?
sentences.zh: 他说，你逗我呢吧？

sentences.en: Because it was, like, a dream for that to be the first thing to do.
sentences.zh: 因为能把这作为第一份工作，简直就像做梦一样。

sentences.en: And also, because it's so many years later now, a lot of people had no idea that I was ever even on there.
sentences.zh: 而且，因为现在已经过去这么多年了，很多人根本不知道我曾经上过那个节目。

sentences.en: And, you know, The Office has had such a continually growing fan base.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，《办公室》的粉丝群一直在不断壮大。

sentences.en: It seems like it had a whole new life all over again, which is great.
sentences.zh: 它好像又焕发了第二次生命，这太棒了。

sentences.en: It's, like, a legacy.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一种传承。

sentences.en: And so people have discovered me on the end, on the end episodes.

sentences.en: It's really funny because it's so unexpected and it's such a nice surprise.

sentences.en: So it just keeps surprising people all these years later.
sentences.zh: 所以这么多年过去了，它依然不断给人们带来惊喜。

sentences.en: So, Angela, since I knew that this was Santi's first on-camera acting job,

sentences.en: I just kind of asked her in general, like, how was that, like, coming onto the set?
sentences.zh: 我就顺便问了她，来到片场感觉怎么样？

sentences.zh: 她讲了一个我觉得你会喜欢的故事。

sentences.en: Here it is.
sentences.zh: 就是这个。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the day of, I remember coming there.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我记得那天去片场的时候。

sentences.en: They told us to wear our own clothes because we were supposed to be playing ourselves.
sentences.zh: 他们让我们穿自己的衣服，因为我们要演自己。

sentences.en: So that part was simple.
sentences.zh: 所以那部分很简单。

sentences.en: And we just got, you know, just got out of hair and makeup and then went in.
sentences.zh: 我们做完妆发，就直接进去了。

sentences.en: And it was just me, Clay Aiken, and Aaron Rodgers.
sentences.zh: 当时只有我、克莱·艾肯和阿隆·罗杰斯。

sentences.en: And I knew who Clay Aiken was, but I did not know who Aaron Rodgers was.
sentences.zh: 我知道克莱·艾肯是谁，但我不知道阿隆·罗杰斯是谁。

sentences.en: And I don't know anything about football.
sentences.zh: 而且我对橄榄球一窍不通。

sentences.en: So I asked him, I said, oh, what do you do?
sentences.zh: 所以我问他，我说，哦，你是做什么的？

sentences.en: And he's like, oh, I'm a football player.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，我是个橄榄球运动员。

sentences.en: And I said, what team do you play for?
sentences.zh: 我说，你效力于哪支球队？

sentences.en: And he said, I believe he said the Green Bay Packers, if that's a team.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果那算是一支球队的话，我记得他说的是绿湾包装工队。

sentences.en: I'm so bad.
sentences.zh: 我真是太糟糕了。

sentences.en: I still don't know about football.
sentences.zh: 我对橄榄球还是不太了解。

sentences.en: And then I asked him, what city was that?
sentences.zh: 然后我问他，那是哪个城市？

sentences.en: And he told me.

sentences.en: And for some reason, I thought he was joking.
sentences.zh: 不知为何，我以为他在开玩笑。

sentences.en: And I was like, no, for real, what city is it?
sentences.zh: 我就说，不，说真的，到底是哪个城市？

sentences.en: And he's like, no, that really is it.
sentences.zh: 他说，不，那真的是那个城市。

sentences.en: So it's kind of a funny intro.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是一个挺有趣的开场。

sentences.en: We ended up getting along really well and having a lot of fun throughout the day.
sentences.zh: 我们最终相处得非常融洽，一整天都过得很开心。

sentences.en: But yeah, it was, I mean, I remember that they were changing the lines a lot, which made me feel a little bit anxious because I'm not used to that.
sentences.zh: 不过确实，我记得他们一直在改台词，这让我有点焦虑，因为我不习惯那样。

sentences.en: And obviously didn't have any experience with that, with, I mean, with any of it at all.
sentences.zh: 显然我对此毫无经验，我是说，对这一切都毫无经验。

sentences.en: It was also new, but like the improvisational aspect was so actually fun to be in and watch Ed Helms just master.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说也是全新的体验，但即兴发挥的部分真的很有趣，能看着艾德·赫尔姆斯（Ed Helms）驾驭自如真是太棒了。

sentences.en: It was so funny.
sentences.zh: 太搞笑了。

sentences.en: And yeah, it was hard not to laugh, but at the same time, it was fun to just be in it with him and just get to experience it and not fall apart.
sentences.zh: 是的，很难不笑场，但与此同时，能和他一起沉浸其中，去体验这一切而不笑场，真的很有趣。

sentences.en: But we did it obviously several times and every time he did it different and every time it was like hilarious.
sentences.zh: 我们显然拍了好几次，他每次演的都不一样，而且每次都特别搞笑。

sentences.en: And so I always, I don't know, I always just really have a fun time watching people who master their crafts and just being able to just be a witness of it.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是，我不知道，我总是很享受观看那些精通自己技艺的人表演，并能亲眼见证这一切。

sentences.zh: 好吧，我们收到了一些关于帕姆正在看的这段蒙太奇的粉丝提问。

sentences.en: One from Randy C.
sentences.zh: 其中一个来自马里兰州哥伦比亚市的兰迪·C，

sentences.en: in Columbia, Maryland, who said,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: Jenna, when filming the sequence where Pam watches the DVD, was there anything really
sentences.zh: 珍娜，在拍摄帕姆观看DVD的片段时，有什么特别的吗？

sentences.en: on the screen or was it put in during post-production?
sentences.zh: 是在屏幕上播放的，还是后期制作时加进去的？

sentences.en: Oh, we also had a fan question from Angela K.
sentences.zh: 哦，我们还收到了一位来自安吉拉·K的粉丝提问。

sentences.en: in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 她来自洛杉矶。

sentences.en: What did she say?
sentences.zh: 她说了什么？

sentences.en: Jenna, were you actually watching the footage in the video?
sentences.zh: 珍娜，你在视频里是真的在看那些片段吗？

sentences.en: And may I also add that your performance in the scene is beautiful and made me tear up.
sentences.zh: 我还要补充一句，你在那场戏里的表演太美了，看得我热泪盈眶。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢。

sentences.en: Well, I'll have you both know, Randy and Angela K., I was watching it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我要告诉你们俩，兰迪和安吉拉·K，我当时确实在看。

sentences.en: And I was watching it for the first time.
sentences.zh: 而且我是第一次看。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: When they started rolling.
sentences.zh: 当他们开始播放的时候。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: I knew what was coming.
sentences.zh: 我知道接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: I knew I was going to see this montage of us as Jim and Pam, but-
sentences.zh: 我知道我会看到我们作为吉姆和帕姆的剪辑片段，但是——

sentences.en: But there's no way to prepare yourself for it.
sentences.zh: 但你根本无法为此做好准备。

sentences.en: There's not.
sentences.zh: 确实无法准备。

sentences.en: Because there were so many wonderful moments.
sentences.zh: 因为里面有太多美好的瞬间了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Sarah R.
sentences.zh: 莎拉·R。

sentences.en: from Cleveland, Ohio, wanted to know who created the video.
sentences.zh: 来自俄亥俄州克利夫兰，她想知道是谁制作了这个视频。

sentences.en: It was Claire Scanlon.
sentences.zh: 是克莱尔·斯坎伦。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: She collected the images.
sentences.zh: 她收集了这些影像。

sentences.en: Dave Rogers gave her a few suggestions.
sentences.zh: 戴夫·罗杰斯给了她一些建议。

sentences.en: There were a few suggestions in the script.
sentences.zh: 剧本里也有一些建议。

sentences.en: She picked out the song, Open Your Eyes, from Snow Patrol.
sentences.zh: 她挑选了雪警乐队的《Open Your Eyes》作为配乐。

sentences.en: Dave said that he believes John Krasinski came in and worked on it a little bit with Claire.
sentences.zh: 戴夫说他相信约翰·卡拉辛斯基也参与进来，和克莱尔一起做了一些调整。

sentences.en: He knew what was on it, but I did not.
sentences.zh: 他知道视频里有什么，但我不知道。

sentences.en: But this was the last scene that we shot for this episode.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是我们这一集拍摄的最后一场戏。

sentences.en: So this was a Friday.
sentences.zh: 所以那是周五。

sentences.en: It was evening.
sentences.zh: 当时是晚上。

sentences.en: It was just us on the set.
sentences.zh: 片场只有我们。

sentences.en: It was very quiet.
sentences.zh: 非常安静。

sentences.en: Really kind of reminded me of when we did Casino Night,
sentences.zh: 真的让我想起了我们拍《赌场之夜》的时候，

sentences.en: when everybody else had gone home and we had like a smaller group for this really emotional moment between these two characters.
sentences.zh: 当时其他人都回家了，我们留下一小群人来拍摄这两个角色之间这个非常感人的时刻。

sentences.en: Well, I'd also love to give a big shout out to Dave Rogers for how he directed this, because I thought it was really beautiful that you watched all of this just heartfelt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我也想特别感谢戴夫·罗杰斯对这场戏的执导，因为我觉得你看着这一切时那种发自内心的情感表达真的很美。

sentences.en: And then Jim is talking to Dwight about Pam at the same time, and Dwight is thinking about Angela.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，吉姆正在和德怀特谈论帕姆，而德怀特在想安吉拉。

sentences.en: When Jim tells Dwight to forget about fear and doubt and do whatever he can to get the one woman who's going to make everything worth it to just do it.
sentences.zh: 当吉姆告诉德怀特要抛开恐惧和怀疑，尽一切努力去争取那个能让一切变得值得的女人，勇敢去做吧。

sentences.en: And he says, you love Angela.
sentences.zh: 他说，你爱安吉拉。

sentences.en: You probably always have.
sentences.zh: 你可能一直都爱她。

sentences.en: And Rain is Dwight.
sentences.zh: 雷恩演的是德怀特。

sentences.en: His performance is brilliant, too.
sentences.zh: 他的表演也很精彩。

sentences.en: So good.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: He's tearing up, and he tells Jim he's a good assistant.
sentences.zh: 他热泪盈眶，还告诉吉姆他是个好助手。

sentences.en: So there's so much emotion happening in these two moments.
sentences.zh: 所以这两个时刻里蕴含了太多的情感。

sentences.en: I thought it was really well done.
sentences.zh: 我觉得处理得非常好。

sentences.en: Well, this whole thing ends with Jim walking back into the break room, seeing that Pam has watched the video, and handing her the original teapot note.
sentences.zh: 好吧，整件事以吉姆走回休息室，看到帕姆看完了视频，并把最初那张茶壶纸条递给她而告终。

sentences.en: The one he took back and put in his pocket all of those years ago.
sentences.zh: 就是他多年前拿回去并放进兜里的那张。

sentences.en: We got a fan question from Lainey B.
sentences.zh: 我们收到了一位来自俄亥俄州韦斯特维尔的粉丝莱尼·B的提问，

sentences.en: in Westerville, Ohio, who said, was it always the plan to revisit the teapot card Jim wrote for Pam?
sentences.zh: 她问，重提吉姆写给帕姆的茶壶纸条，这是否一直都在计划之中？

sentences.en: Or was it something that the writers remembered and wanted to incorporate into the episode?
sentences.zh: 还是说这是编剧们后来想起来，想要加进剧集里的内容？

sentences.en: Lainey, it was not always planned.
sentences.zh: 莱妮，这并不是一开始就计划好的。

sentences.en: Like, not from when we did that first Christmas episode did anybody say, one day we're going to reveal what was on this note.
sentences.zh: 比如，并不是从我们拍第一集圣诞特辑时，就有人说，总有一天我们要揭晓那张纸条上写了什么。

sentences.en: It sort of took on a life of its own.
sentences.zh: 它算是自己演变出了生命力。

sentences.en: People became so curious what was in the note that Jim didn't give Pam.
sentences.zh: 大家对吉姆没给帕姆的那张纸条里写了什么变得非常好奇。

sentences.en: And I've told this story before, but when we were pitching to Greg about season nine, I said, Greg, we have to read the teapot note.
sentences.zh: 我以前讲过这个故事，但当我们向格雷格提议第九季的构思时，我说，格雷格，我们必须读一下那个茶壶纸条。

sentences.en: I mean, it's the greatest callback of the whole series.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是整部剧最棒的呼应了。

sentences.en: It's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这太绝了。

sentences.en: This is a fantastic idea.
sentences.zh: 这真是个绝妙的主意。

sentences.en: Did they lose their minds when you pitched it?
sentences.zh: 当你提议的时候，他们有没有激动得疯掉？

sentences.en: Well, I felt like I kind of had to convince them a little bit because—
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得我当时还得稍微说服他们一下，因为——

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: Here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 是这样的。

sentences.en: Greg said, I don't think we'll ever be able to write anything that would satisfy everybody's imagination of this note after all these years.
sentences.zh: 格雷格说，我不认为我们写出的任何内容，能在这么多年后满足所有人对这张纸条的想象。

sentences.en: Like, the beauty of the note is that as the audience member, you've written the perfect thing on the note.
sentences.zh: 因为这张纸条的魅力在于，作为观众，你已经在心里写下了最完美的答案。

sentences.en: That's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 那太聪明了。

sentences.en: I mean, he's so smart, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他真的很聪明，对吧？

sentences.en: That is a very smart take.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常高明的见解。

sentences.en: But it's enough for me to just see it.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，只要能看到它就足够了。

sentences.en: Well, that was the thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，关键就在这儿。

sentences.en: We didn't have to read it to you.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要读给你听。

sentences.en: You just needed the satisfaction of Pam getting it.
sentences.zh: 你只需要看到帕姆收到它，就能获得满足感。

sentences.en: She finally gets it.
sentences.zh: 她终于收到了。

sentences.en: Of Pam reading it.
sentences.zh: 看到帕姆读它。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then you still get to fill in the blank, but you get that closure.
sentences.zh: 这样你依然可以保留自己的想象空间，但同时也得到了那种圆满感。

sentences.en: I've told this story before, too.
sentences.zh: 我也讲过这个故事。

sentences.en: But John Krasinski wrote the note.
sentences.zh: 那张纸条是约翰·卡拉辛斯基写的。

sentences.en: It was a private note.
sentences.zh: 那是一张私人的纸条。

sentences.en: That he wrote to you as Jenna.
sentences.zh: 是他写给作为珍娜的你的。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: About being your scene partner all those years.
sentences.zh: 关于这些年来作为你搭档的感受。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it was kind of like a goodbye, thank you note.
sentences.zh: 所以那更像是一封告别和感谢的信。

sentences.en: I still have it.
sentences.zh: 我至今还留着它。

sentences.en: It's private.
sentences.zh: 它是私人的。

sentences.en: I'll never reveal what was in it.
sentences.zh: 我永远不会透露里面写了什么。

sentences.en: But it was a beautiful, beautiful note from one scene partner to another.
sentences.zh: 但那是一封非常、非常美丽的信，来自一位搭档对另一位搭档的寄语。

sentences.en: It made me cry.
sentences.zh: 它让我哭了。

sentences.en: So when you see me crying in the episode, those are my real tears.
sentences.zh: 所以当你在剧里看到我哭的时候，那是我真实的眼泪。

sentences.en: I did notice when you were reading it, it seemed like some genuine surprise that you didn't know what was going to be given to you.
sentences.zh: 我确实注意到你读的时候，看起来有一种真实的惊讶，因为你不知道会收到什么。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They told me they were going to let John write the note, but I thought he was going to write it as Jim to Pam.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我他们会让约翰写这张纸条，但我以为他会以吉姆的身份写给帕姆。

sentences.en: So as I'm reading it and I'm realizing that it says, Dear Jenna,
sentences.zh: 所以当我读到它，意识到上面写着“亲爱的珍娜”时，

sentences.en: and then it's just this beautiful letter about what it has meant for us to work together and be these scene partners.
sentences.zh: 然后接着就是那封关于我们一起工作、作为搭档意味着什么的优美信件。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's like to be Jim and Pam.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，就像是作为吉姆和帕姆的感受。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I was like, oh, my gosh.
sentences.zh: 我当时心想，天哪。

sentences.en: Oh, oh, my goodness.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You see your face goes through a bunch of realizations.
sentences.zh: 你看得出你的表情经历了一连串的心理活动。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think you can see John watching me read it.
sentences.zh: 而且我想你能看到约翰在看着我读那封信。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think you see him.
sentences.zh: 我想你能看到他。

sentences.en: For sure.
sentences.zh: 肯定的。

sentences.en: Like, okay, I'm standing here as she reads this letter.
sentences.zh: 就像是，好吧，我就站在这儿看着她读这封信。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, I agree with Greg.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我同意格雷格的看法。

sentences.en: I'm glad you've never shared what you actually read, what was from John to you, because I don't want to break that fourth wall.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你从未透露过你当时读到的内容，也就是约翰写给你的那些话，因为我不想打破那层“第四面墙”。

sentences.en: I want to imagine this moment between Jim and Pam, and I want to imagine what I would have wanted Jim to say.
sentences.zh: 我想保留吉姆和帕姆之间那一刻的想象空间，也想保留我当时希望吉姆说出的话。

sentences.en: Well, as a wrap gift at the finale, I wanted to return the favor.
sentences.zh: 嗯，作为大结局的杀青礼物，我想礼尚往来。

sentences.en: So I bought a little teapot, and I wrote a note to John from Jenna, my own little teapot note to him, thanking him for all those years working together and what it had meant to me.
sentences.zh: 所以我买了一个小茶壶，并以珍娜的名义给约翰写了一张字条，这是我写给他的专属“茶壶字条”，感谢他多年来的合作以及这段经历对我而言的意义。

sentences.en: I mean, I'll never have a scene partner like that again.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我再也不会有那样的搭档了。

sentences.en: I feel like I have a work partner and a creative partner like that here with you, Angela.
sentences.zh: 我觉得安吉拉，在这里和你一起工作，我也拥有了同样的工作伙伴和创作伙伴。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: This is like another moment of, like, chemistry that you just – you can't plan for it.
sentences.zh: 这就像是另一种化学反应，你根本无法预先计划。

sentences.en: It's just, like, it's perfect.
sentences.zh: 简直太完美了。

sentences.en: But to go on a nine-year journey with another actor in such an intimate and vulnerable way, as our characters do, it's pretty special.
sentences.zh: 但能和另一位演员以如此亲密和脆弱的方式共同走过九年的旅程，就像我们的角色所做的那样，这真的很特别。

sentences.en: I mean, we're bonded for life, for sure.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们注定要羁绊一生，这是肯定的。

sentences.en: For sure.
sentences.zh: 肯定的。

sentences.en: It's nine years.
sentences.zh: 那是九年啊。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Yeah, I feel the same way.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我有同感。

sentences.en: And, you know, we reached out to Dave about this episode, and he shared something about this scene, about how they would cut from Jim and Dwight back to Pam.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们为了这一集联系了戴夫，他分享了一些关于这个场景的事情，比如他们是如何从吉姆和德怀特的镜头切回帕姆的。

sentences.en: And it's something he fought for, and that was to keep the music playing under the cutaways.
sentences.zh: 这是他极力争取的，那就是在切换镜头时保持音乐持续播放。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And at first, I guess Greg wanted to take it out whenever they cut to Jim and Dwight.
sentences.zh: 起初，我猜格雷格想在切到吉姆和德怀特时把音乐关掉。

sentences.en: But Claire agreed with Dave, and they said it would be a great tool that the documentary filmmakers could use to underscore these two moments.
sentences.zh: 但克莱尔同意戴夫的看法，他们认为这将是纪录片制作人用来强调这两个时刻的绝佳手段。

sentences.en: And he really felt like it tied the two scenes together.
sentences.zh: 他真的觉得这样能把两个场景联系在一起。

sentences.en: And ultimately, Greg agreed, and they kept the music throughout both scenes.
sentences.zh: 最终，格雷格同意了，他们让音乐贯穿了两个场景。

sentences.en: And I do think it tied them together beautifully.
sentences.zh: 我也确实认为这把它们完美地串联了起来。

sentences.en: So there's one more thing about this scene that caused quite a stir after it aired.
sentences.zh: 关于这个场景还有一件事，在播出后引起了不小的轰动。

sentences.en: And it all has to do with a little mistake that they made.
sentences.zh: 这一切都源于他们犯的一个小错误。

sentences.en: You know that very first slide of the little slideshow where Jim has written a note to Pam?
sentences.zh: 你知道那个小幻灯片的第一张，吉姆给帕姆写了张字条吗？

sentences.en: Yes, he wrote Beasley,
sentences.zh: 是的，他写的是“比斯利”，

sentences.en: You think I'll have regrets.
sentences.zh: “你以为我会后悔。”

sentences.en: I asked the doc crew to help me show you why I won't dot, dot, dot.
sentences.zh: “我请纪录片摄制组帮我向你展示为什么我不会……点点点。”

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Well, when this episode first aired, Pam's last name was misspelled.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当这一集刚播出时，帕姆的姓氏拼错了。

sentences.en: It was spelled B-E-E-S-L-E-Y.
sentences.zh: 拼成了 B-E-E-S-L-E-Y。

sentences.en: But that's not how you spell Beasley.
sentences.zh: 但比斯利（Beasley）不是那样拼的。

sentences.en: You spell it B-E-E-S-L-Y.
sentences.zh: 应该是 B-E-E-S-L-Y。

sentences.en: Mm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: No E.
sentences.zh: 没有 E。

sentences.en: No E.
sentences.zh: 没有 E。

sentences.en: And fans were like, Jim misspelled his wife's name in the love tribute video.
sentences.zh: 粉丝们当时就说，吉姆在爱的致敬视频里把妻子的名字拼错了。

sentences.en: But then people started arguing over what is the correct spelling of Pam's last name.
sentences.zh: 但后来人们开始争论帕姆的姓氏到底该怎么拼。

sentences.en: There's been several versions online.
sentences.zh: 网上已经有好几个版本了。

sentences.en: Well, here's what I can tell you.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我能告诉你们的是这些。

sentences.en: In the very first page of every script, there's a cast liSt.
sentences.zh: 在每一份剧本的第一页，都有演员表。

sentences.en: And from script number one to script finale, Pam's last name has always been spelled B-E-E-S-L-Y.
sentences.zh: 从第一集剧本到最后一集，帕姆的姓氏拼写一直都是B-E-E-S-L-Y。

sentences.en: That's how Greg intended it.
sentences.zh: 那是格雷格原本的意图。

sentences.en: However, it is misspelled a couple of times in early episodes.
sentences.zh: 不过，在早期剧集中确实有几次拼错了。

sentences.en: And then in this episode, but in business school at her art fair, it's spelled correctly in the credits for Threat Level Midnight.
sentences.zh: 然后在这一集里，在商学院那集的艺术展上，在《威胁等级：午夜》的演职员表中，拼写是正确的。

sentences.en: It's spelled correctly on the big poster outside their wedding where they misspelled Jim's last name, Halprit.
sentences.zh: 在他们婚礼外面的大横幅上拼写也是正确的，虽然那里把吉姆的姓氏拼成了Halprit。

sentences.en: Her name is spelled correctly.
sentences.zh: 她的名字拼写是正确的。

sentences.en: So that is the correct spelling.
